section: Rights of persons with disabilities - RPwD Act 2016, UNCRPD, accessibility (Sugamya Bharat)
subsections: Accessible India Campaign (Sugamya Bharat Abhiyan) - launch, verticals, app
Special and inclusive education - RCI Act 1992, Samagra Shiksha inclusive education, special education target groups

accepted.s: The Accessible India Campaign was launched on which date?
accepted.x: The Accessible India Campaign was launched on 3 December 2015 as a flagship initiative for universal accessibility.
accepted.tq: Use the exact launch date rather than confusing it with an observance date.
accepted.sec: Accessible India Campaign (Sugamya Bharat Abhiyan) - launch, verticals, app  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly represents the three verticals of the Accessible India Campaign?
o: Transport system, social security and vocational training
Built environment, transport system and ICT ecosystem
Built environment, electoral reforms and digital payments
Health services, education system and rural housing
accepted.x: The three verticals are accessibility in the built environment, transport system and ICT ecosystem.
accepted.tq: Identify the complete official triad and reject neighbouring disability-welfare activities.
accepted.sec: Accessible India Campaign (Sugamya Bharat Abhiyan) - launch, verticals, app  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the Accessible India Campaign:
1. It was launched in 2015.
2. It is associated with the Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities.
3. Its verticals include the built environment, transport and ICT.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The campaign was launched in 2015, is associated with DEPwD and has the three stated accessibility verticals.
accepted.tq: Check whether the institutional association and the three-part structure are both retained.
accepted.sec: Accessible India Campaign (Sugamya Bharat Abhiyan) - launch, verticals, app  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Sugamya Bharat App is primarily a platform for which of the following?
o: Providing monthly pensions to persons with disabilities
accepted.x: The Sugamya Bharat App functions as a crowdsourcing platform through which accessibility gaps can be reported.
accepted.tq: Match the digital application with its operational function, not with another disability service.
accepted.sec: Accessible India Campaign (Sugamya Bharat Abhiyan) - launch, verticals, app  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: UDID — single national disability ID and certificate
SIPDA — monthly pension to BPL households
accepted.x: UDID provides a single national disability identity and certificate. SIPDA, DDRS and PM-DAKSH have different functions.
accepted.tq: Use the exact institutional function to distinguish identity, grants and training schemes.
accepted.sec: Accessible India Campaign (Sugamya Bharat Abhiyan) - launch, verticals, app  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Unified Disability Identity (UDID) is intended to provide which of the following?
o: A grant exclusively to rehabilitation NGOs
A monthly pension only to persons below the poverty line
A transport concession card issued only by APSRTC
A single, digitally verifiable national disability card
accepted.x: UDID is a single, digitally verifiable national disability card and certificate.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between a national identity system and benefit-specific schemes.

accepted.s:
Which of the following statements regarding accessible elections is correct?
1. Accessible elections include accessible polling booths.
2. Braille-enabled EVMs are associated with accessible elections.
3. Accessible elections are one of the three verticals of the Accessible India Campaign.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Accessible booths and Braille-enabled EVMs are measures for accessible elections. Accessible elections are not listed as one of the three campaign verticals; the verticals are built environment, transport and ICT.
accepted.tq: Separate a related accessibility measure from the officially listed campaign verticals.
accepted.sec: Accessible India Campaign (Sugamya Bharat Abhiyan) - launch, verticals, app  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Supreme Court recognised safe footpaths as a fundamental right under which Article, along with a minimum footpath width of 1.8 metres?
accepted.x: The Supreme Court recognised safe footpaths as part of the right to life under Article 21 and specified a minimum width of 1.8 metres.
accepted.tq: Link the judicially recognised right with the correct constitutional Article and measurement.
accepted.sec: Accessible India Campaign (Sugamya Bharat Abhiyan) - launch, verticals, app  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Under the Andhra Pradesh initiative named ‘Indra Dhanassu’, free APSRTC bus travel is available to persons with disabilities having at least what percentage of disability?
accepted.x: From 18 March 2026, free APSRTC bus travel is available in the specified categories to persons with 40 percent or more disability.
accepted.tq: Focus on the eligibility threshold rather than the separate escort concession.
accepted.sec: Accessible India Campaign (Sugamya Bharat Abhiyan) - launch, verticals, app  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Under the Andhra Pradesh free bus travel initiative for persons with disabilities, an escort is entitled to which concession?
accepted.x: An escort receives a 50 percent concession under the stated AP bus travel initiative.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the beneficiary’s full concession from the escort’s partial concession.
accepted.sec: Accessible India Campaign (Sugamya Bharat Abhiyan) - launch, verticals, app  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The International Year of Disabled Persons was observed in:
accepted.x: The International Year of Disabled Persons was observed in 1981.
accepted.tq: Distinguish an international year from an annual observance or statutory enactment year.

accepted.s: Which scheme provides free aids and appliances to eligible persons below a monthly income of Rs 22,500 and subsidised assistance up to Rs 30,000?
accepted.x: The ADIP scheme provides free aids and appliances to persons below the stated income limit and subsidised assistance up to Rs 30,000.
accepted.tq: Match the income ceiling and assistance limit with the correct scheme.

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: PM-DAKSH — skill training and job linkage
IGNDPS — monthly pension to severely disabled persons from BPL households
SIPDA — free aids and appliances below a specified income ceiling
DDRS — grants to NGOs for rehabilitation and vocational training
accepted.x: SIPDA provides grant-in-aid for implementing the RPwD Act. Free aids and appliances are associated with ADIP.
accepted.tq: Find the scheme whose benefit has been swapped with that of ADIP.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. DDRS provides grants to NGOs for rehabilitation.
2. PM-DAKSH is associated with skill training and job linkage for persons with disabilities.
3. IGNDPS provides a monthly pension to severely disabled persons from BPL households.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements correctly state the principal benefits of DDRS, PM-DAKSH and IGNDPS.
accepted.tq: Verify each scheme against its distinct beneficiary service before selecting the combined code.

accepted.s: The ADIP scheme provides aids and appliances and corrective surgery through which combination of institutions?
o: Universities, Bhavitha Centres, SADAREM and NSAP
accepted.x: ADIP operates through institutions including National Institutes, Composite Regional Centres, ALIMCO and District Disability Rehabilitation Centres.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure institutional pair and identify the complete delivery network.

accepted.s: Which scheme gives grants to States, bodies and universities for implementing the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act?
accepted.x: SIPDA provides grants to States, bodies and universities for implementation of the RPwD Act.
accepted.tq: Identify the implementation grant scheme rather than the rehabilitation or pension scheme.

accepted.s:
Which of the following is NOT a component of the Scholarships for Students with Disabilities scheme?
1. Pre-matric scholarship
2. Post-matric scholarship
3. National Fellowship
4. Monthly disability pension
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Monthly disability pension is not one of the six scholarship components. The listed components include pre-matric, post-matric and National Fellowship, along with Top Class, Overseas and Free Coaching.
accepted.tq: Find the welfare benefit that does not belong to a scholarship-component list.

accepted.s: In Andhra Pradesh, the number of District Disability Rehabilitation Centres and NGOs under DDRS is respectively:
accepted.x: Andhra Pradesh has 9 DDRCs and 70 NGOs under DDRS.
accepted.tq: Preserve the order of the two quantities while rejecting nearby disability figures.

accepted.s: According to Census 2011, persons with disabilities constituted what proportion of India’s population?
accepted.x: Census 2011 recorded 2.68 crore persons with disabilities, constituting 2.21 percent of India’s population.
accepted.tq: Match the percentage with the corresponding census count instead of the global estimate.

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly compares the Census 2011 figure for India with the approximate global estimate mentioned for persons with disabilities?
o: India: 2.21 percent; global estimate: about 16 percent
India: about 16 percent; global estimate: 2.21 percent
accepted.x: India’s Census 2011 figure was 2.21 percent, whereas the approximate global estimate was about 16 percent; the difference suggests under-reporting in India.
accepted.tq: Keep national census data separate from the international estimate and disability-type percentages.

accepted.s: Among the following categories, which was the largest disability group in India according to the cited Census 2011 distribution?
accepted.x: Movement disability was the largest among the cited categories at 20.3 percent, followed by hearing at 18.9 percent and seeing at 18.8 percent.
accepted.tq: Compare the three close percentages rather than relying on a broad category impression.

accepted.s:
Arrange the following disability categories in descending order according to their cited shares in India:
A. Movement
B. Hearing
C. Seeing
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: The shares are movement 20.3 percent, hearing 18.9 percent and seeing 18.8 percent; therefore, the order is A, B, C.
accepted.tq: Order close numerical values by comparing the decimal figures carefully.

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly represents the distribution of persons with disabilities in Andhra Pradesh according to the cited Census 2011 figures?
o: Hearing 3.13 lakh, orthopaedic 2.90 lakh and visual 2.03 lakh
Orthopaedic 3.13 lakh, hearing 2.90 lakh and visual 2.03 lakh
Visual 3.13 lakh, hearing 2.03 lakh and orthopaedic 2.90 lakh
Orthopaedic 2.03 lakh, visual 2.90 lakh and hearing 3.13 lakh
accepted.x: The cited AP figures are 3.13 lakh orthopaedic, 2.90 lakh hearing and 2.03 lakh visual disabilities.
accepted.tq: Match each category with its exact numerical value and preserve the ranking.

accepted.s: Which one of the following is the correct descending order of the cited disability categories in Andhra Pradesh?
accepted.x: The figures are orthopaedic 3.13 lakh, hearing 2.90 lakh, visual 2.03 lakh, multiple 1.96 lakh and mental 1.02 lakh.
accepted.tq: Use the descending numerical order to test the complete AP category ranking.

accepted.s: Under the Andhra Pradesh Divyang Shakti free bus travel arrangement, disability certification is carried out through:
accepted.x: The cited Andhra Pradesh arrangement uses SADAREM for disability certification.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the state certification system from national identity, training and screening platforms.

accepted.s:
Which of the following statements about the Andhra Pradesh welfare measures is correct?
1. Inclusive education assistance is Rs 3,500 per child with special needs.
2. Andhra Pradesh has 679 Bhavitha Centres.
3. The Andhra Pradesh Samagra Shiksha programme received the national award for Best State in implementing the RPwD Act for 2024-25.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: All three statements are correct: the assistance is Rs 3,500 per child, there are 679 Bhavitha Centres, and AP received the stated national award for 2024-25.
accepted.tq: Combine the monetary, institutional and award facts without confusing them with national scheme data.

accepted.s: The Andhra Pradesh Differently Abled and Senior Citizens Assistance Corporation primarily performs which functions?
o: Supplying aids and appliances and running economic-rehabilitation schemes
Conducting the Census and issuing national disability cards
Providing only international scholarships to persons with disabilities
Regulating rehabilitation professionals and maintaining the Central Rehabilitation Register
accepted.x: The Corporation supplies aids and appliances and runs economic-rehabilitation schemes for persons with disabilities and senior citizens.
accepted.tq: Identify the state welfare corporation by its paired functions rather than by a statutory regulatory role.

accepted.s:
Match the following cases with the issue involved:
 a. Jeeja Ghosh v. Union of India
 b. Vikash Kumar v. UPSC
 c. Rajive Raturi v. Union of India

 i. Scribe as reasonable accommodation without benchmark disability
 ii. Mandatory accessibility standards under the RPwD Act
 iii. Deplaning of a woman with cerebral palsy and right to dignity

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Jeeja Ghosh concerned deplaning and dignity; Vikash Kumar recognised a scribe as reasonable accommodation; Rajive Raturi concerned mandatory accessibility standards.
accepted.tq: Start with the distinctive case issue and then eliminate the codes with swapped judgments.

accepted.s: In Jeeja Ghosh v. Union of India, the principal issue concerned:
o: The maintenance of the Central Rehabilitation Register
A candidate’s entitlement to a scribe without benchmark disability
The framing of mandatory accessibility standards under the RPwD Act
A woman with cerebral palsy being deplaned by an airline and her right to dignity
accepted.x: Jeeja Ghosh concerned the deplaning of a woman with cerebral palsy by an airline, raising the right to dignity and resulting in compensation.
accepted.tq: Associate the case with its distinctive factual incident rather than a general accessibility principle.

accepted.s: Which case recognised a scribe as a form of reasonable accommodation even in the absence of benchmark disability?
o: Jeeja Ghosh v. Union of India
Rajive Raturi v. Union of India
accepted.x: Vikash Kumar v. UPSC (2021) recognised the availability of a scribe as reasonable accommodation even without benchmark disability.
accepted.tq: Use the specific accommodation to distinguish the case from dignity and accessibility-standard cases.

accepted.s: Rajive Raturi v. Union of India (2024) was associated with which issue?
o: Compensation for deplaning a passenger with cerebral palsy
Recognition of an International Year of Disabled Persons
Mandatory accessibility standards to be framed under the RPwD Act
accepted.x: The case concerned mandatory accessibility standards to be framed under the RPwD Act.
accepted.tq: Match the judicial direction with the subject-specific accessibility issue.

accepted.s: The Rehabilitation Council of India Act, 1992 provided for the establishment of which body?
accepted.x: The RCI Act, 1992 established the Rehabilitation Council of India, which became statutory from 1993.
accepted.tq: Match the statute with the body created by it, avoiding similarly named professional councils.
accepted.sec: Special and inclusive education - RCI Act 1992, Samagra Shiksha inclusive education, special education target groups  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes the Rehabilitation Council of India?
o: It regulates training of rehabilitation and special-education professionals and maintains the Central Rehabilitation Register.
It operates only the Sugamya Bharat crowdsourcing application.
It conducts the decennial Census of persons with disabilities.
It provides only monthly pensions to severely disabled persons from BPL households.
accepted.x: The RCI regulates training of rehabilitation and special-education professionals and maintains the Central Rehabilitation Register.
accepted.tq: Identify the regulator’s professional and registration functions instead of assigning it welfare or data functions.
accepted.sec: Special and inclusive education - RCI Act 1992, Samagra Shiksha inclusive education, special education target groups  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Special education under the cited framework primarily targets:
o: All adult learners undertaking vocational training
accepted.x: The target group for special education is children with disabilities, or CwSN; it is not a programme exclusively for gifted groups.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between children with disabilities and the misleading alternative of gifted children.
accepted.sec: Special and inclusive education - RCI Act 1992, Samagra Shiksha inclusive education, special education target groups  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Which of the following services is covered under Samagra Shiksha’s inclusive education component for RPwD-listed disabilities?
1. Assessment
2. Aids and assistive technology
3. Therapy
4. Exclusive education of gifted children
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Samagra Shiksha covers assessment, aids, assistive technology and therapy for children with disabilities. Exclusive education of gifted children is not its stated target.
accepted.tq: Find the unrelated target group while retaining the complete inclusive-education service package.
accepted.sec: Special and inclusive education - RCI Act 1992, Samagra Shiksha inclusive education, special education target groups  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Samagra Shiksha’s inclusive education component took over which earlier programme?
accepted.x: The inclusive education component of Samagra Shiksha took over the earlier IEDSS programme.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the predecessor education programme from disability rehabilitation and pension schemes.
accepted.sec: Special and inclusive education - RCI Act 1992, Samagra Shiksha inclusive education, special education target groups  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about Andhra Pradesh’s inclusive education measures:
1. The Zero Rejection Policy is followed.
2. Assistance of Rs 3,500 is provided per child with special needs.
3. The number of CwSN enrolled is 16,238.
4. There are 679 Bhavitha Centres.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements correctly state the cited Andhra Pradesh inclusive-education measures and figures.
accepted.tq: Check each numerical and policy detail before selecting the complete combination.
accepted.sec: Special and inclusive education - RCI Act 1992, Samagra Shiksha inclusive education, special education target groups  [APPSC, GROUP-II]
